- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There were certainly young women and girls who made important contributions throughout history before Sybil Ludington.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of young women and girls include Joan of Arc, Artemisia I of Caria, Pocahontas, Mary Jones, and Mirabai.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Joan of Arc (1412 CE - 1431 CE): a French heroine who led the French army to several victories during the Hundred Years' War. She was captured and executed by the English for heresy at the age of 19.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Artemisia I of Caria (fl. 480 BCE): a queen of Caria who fought alongside the Persians against the Greeks in the Battle of Salamis.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pocahontas (1596 CE - 1617 CE): a Native American woman who played a critical role in the early history of the English settlement at Jamestown, Virginia.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mary Jones (1784 CE - 1864 CE): a Welsh girl who, at the age of 16, walked 25 miles to purchase a copy of the Bible in Welsh.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mirabai (1498 CE - 1547 CE): a medieval Indian poet and mystic who composed devotional poetry in the Bhakti tradition.
- [USER] Asked if all the examples provided were under 18.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Apologized for the confusion and clarified that not all examples were under 18.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Provided additional examples of young women and girls who made significant contributions before the age of 18, including Sacagawea, Mary Shelley, Anne Frank, and Claudette Colvin.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Sacagawea (1788 CE - 1812 CE): a Shoshone woman who, at the age of 16, accompanied the Lewis and Clark expedition across the western United States.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mary Shelley (1797 CE - 1851 CE): an English writer who wrote the classic novel "Frankenstein" when she was just 18 years old.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Anne Frank (1929 CE - 1945 CE): a young Jewish girl who wrote a diary while hiding with her family during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Claudette Colvin (1939 CE - present): an American civil rights activist who, at the age of 15, refused to give up her seat on a bus in Montgomery, Alabama.
